# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — breadth pass: 3 code fixes + 4 prompt rules across 5 failing clusters
- Changes I made (file/tool + cluster):
  1. tools.py `cancel_reservation` — in-body guard: raise if any flight.date < current date (cluster 3, task 37: extra wrong cancel of already-flown NQNU5R).
  2. tools.py `book_reservation` — payment auto-resolve: single method → set to total; one credit card among several → absorbs remainder; re-sync payment_history; else actionable error (cluster 1, tasks 25/8: payment-sum stall).
  3. tools.py NEW `list_reservations(user_id)` — loop tool returning per-reservation route/date/cabin/pax summaries (cluster 2, tasks 17/22: wrong reservation selected).
  4. policy.md "How to execute write actions" — confirm once → next output MUST be the write call; retry in-turn on fixable errors; never claim success without a returned call; 2 worked examples (cluster 1, tasks 8/25/40).
  5. policy.md "Finding the right reservation" — use list_reservations + match by route, never assume first (cluster 2).
  6. policy.md "Change passengers" — pass FULL passenger list after get_reservation_details (cluster 4, task 40).
  7. policy.md Modify→Payment — report exact charge/refund from payment_history newest entry, not a search estimate (cluster 5, task 11).
- Expected effect + why safe: each edit targets a currently-failing write. All are bounded — the cancel guard fires only on past-dated flights, the payment auto-resolve only on a sum mismatch, list_reservations is additive read-only, and the prompt rules are additive (loosen no deny/refuse rule). The one passing task (12) is a baggage update with a reservation id supplied and confirmed-once-then-acted; no passing task books, cancels, or does route-lookup, so passing behavior is unchanged.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — first iteration; LEDGER/JOURNAL/RUNMAP/prior_iterations all empty.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet (no prior RESULTs).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: task 19 (should-cancel basic-economy — trigger not safely determinable from the trace; a global rule would be an unbounded decision change). Task 23 is infra noise (max_steps null).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this iteration's RESULT is flat, the next lever to try is inspecting the eval task-DB states directly (this run's local base DB differs from eval), and designing the task-19 cancel trigger from flight statuses rather than prose.
- Focus next iteration: read this entry's RESULT line; keep whatever it marks fixed, redesign whatever it marks broke, then crack task 19 and re-examine any COMMUNICATE-only failures.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.667 Δ=+0.567 · fixed={11, 17, 19, 25, 40, 8} · broke={12} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (first iteration)
- Strategy tried: breadth-first. Diagnosed all 9 failing traces, clustered by root cause, and shipped one bounded fix per cluster (3 code + 4 prompt) rather than over-investing in the single biggest cluster. Whether it moved val: unknown until this candidate's RESULT is stamped (no LEDGER rows yet).
- Method that worked well procedurally: (a) parse traces into user-turns + agent tool-calls + gold action_checks + feedback to see the EXACT wrong write; (b) verify tool-body logic against CONTROLLED inputs in the tau2 venv, because the local base get_db() differs from the eval task-DBs (dates/prices). Guessing from base DB alone would have been misleading (e.g. NQNU5R is future-dated locally but past-dated in eval task 37).
- Preferred CODE over prose wherever a rule could be enforced deterministically (cancel guard, payment auto-resolve, list_reservations) — the mid model narrates rules but doesn't reliably execute them, so a tool that just does the right thing is higher-leverage than a paragraph telling it to.
- Plateau/stall signal: n/a (first iteration).
- What to try next iteration: (1) read the RESULT line and keep fixed / redesign broke; (2) the biggest un-de-risked assumption is that eval task-DB states match my logic — a future iteration should locate and inspect the actual eval task DBs; (3) crack task 19 (should-cancel basic-economy) by deriving the trigger from flight statuses, not prose; (4) if code fixes plateau, switch lever to COMMUNICATE-only failures (amounts/wording) which prompt rules address.

- The proposer's local base DB (`get_db()` / AIRLINE_DB_PATH) does NOT match the per-task eval DB states (flight dates, prices, and which reservations exist differ — e.g. NQNU5R is future-dated locally but past-dated in eval task 37; task 25 re-quotes the fare to 375). SUGGESTION: expose each eval task's initial DB snapshot (read-only) to the proposer, or at least the per-task overrides applied on top of the base DB, so a fix can be verified against the exact state it will be scored on.
- The failing traces include a null-reward task caused by hitting max_steps (task 23). This is indistinguishable from a genuine capability failure without opening the trace. SUGGESTION: tag rollouts that terminated on the step cap / infra error separately from reward-0 capability failures, so proposers don't spend an edit on infra noise.

# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Domain: tau2-bench airline. Runtime reader: aws/gpt-oss-120b (mid-capability). Parent = seed
(val reward 0.100, 1 passing task 12, 9 failing). This is iteration 1 (no prior iterations).
Every failure is a DB-state mismatch on a WRITE action. I read all 9 failing traces, clustered
them by root cause, and shipped one fix per cluster passing REAL/SAFE/VERIFIED. I preferred CODE
(deterministic tool enforcement) over prose for behavioral/rule-violation/capability clusters.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Action stall — narrate the write, never call the tool (or don't retry after a fixable error) | 8, 25, 40 | Agent prints a summary, user confirms + ###STOP###, but the write tool is never called. Task 25 also mis-summed payment ($299 vs $375) then described the fix instead of re-calling. | BEHAVIORAL + CAPABILITY-GAP | prompt execution-discipline rules + book_reservation payment auto-resolve (code) |
| 2 | Wrong reservation selected | 17, 22 | User named a trip by route/city; agent acted on a non-matching reservation instead of the described one. No one-call way to list a user's reservations by route. | CAPABILITY-GAP | new `list_reservations` tool (code) + lookup-by-route prompt rule |
| 3 | Cancelled an already-flown reservation | 37 | Agent cancelled NQNU5R whose flights (05-13/14) are before current date 05-15 → an EXTRA wrong write. Gold has NO cancel; only the M20IZO upgrade was correct. | RULE-VIOLATION | in-body guard on cancel_reservation (code) |
| 4 | Passenger update dropped/mis-set the full list | 40 (+17,22) | update_reservation_passengers REPLACES the whole list; agent must include unchanged passengers after reading current details. | KNOWLEDGE | prompt procedure rule |
| 5 | Refund/charge amount mis-communicated | 11 | Agent reported an amount computed from current search prices, not the tool's actual payment_history delta. | KNOWLEDGE | prompt rule: report payment_history delta |
| — | Should-cancel basic-economy | 19 | Gold cancels a basic-economy reservation; the safe general trigger isn't determinable from the trace. | — | deliberately skipped |
| — | max_steps null | 23 | Rollout hit the step cap; uninformative zero. | — | skipped (infra) |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | in-body guard | tools.py `cancel_reservation` | Raise if any `flight.date < self._get_datetime()[:10]`. General "already flown → cannot cancel, transfer instead" per policy. | Yes — fires only on past-dated flights; task 12 doesn't cancel; future-dated reservations unaffected. |
| 1 | in-body computation + actionable error | tools.py `book_reservation` | If payment amounts ≠ total_price: single method → set it to total; one credit card among several → credit absorbs the remainder. Re-sync `payment_history` to adjusted amounts. Else raise a directive error naming the exact total. | Yes — fires only on a sum-mismatch; no passing task books; correct splits untouched. |
| 2 | new READ/loop tool | tools.py `list_reservations(user_id)` | Loops the user's reservations → compact route/date/cabin/passenger summaries in ONE call so the model matches by route instead of guessing. | Yes — purely additive read-only tool. |
| 1 | prompt (procedure + 2 worked examples) | policy.md "How to execute write actions" | Confirm ONCE, then the very next output MUST be the write call; retry in-turn after a fixable error; never claim success without a returned call. | Yes — loosens no refuse/deny rule; task 12 already confirmed-once-then-acted. |
| 2 | prompt rule | policy.md "Finding the right reservation" | Use list_reservations and match origin/destination/date; never assume the first reservation. | Yes — only triggers when no reservation ID was given (additive). |
| 4 | prompt rule | policy.md "Change passengers" | Pass the FULL passenger list (get_reservation_details first); edit only the requested passenger(s). | Yes — additive knowledge. |
| 5 | prompt rule | policy.md Modify→Payment | Report the exact charge/refund from the returned payment_history newest entry, not a search-price estimate. | Yes — additive; task 12 is a baggage update, unaffected. |

## Verify-the-fix (trace targeted → what the guard/computation/new-tool does on those inputs)
- cancel_reservation (task 37): NQNU5R flights set to 05-13/14 → RAISES "already departed"; future-dated reservations (05-16/17, 05-28) → NO raise. Blast radius: only past-dated cancels.
- book_reservation (task 25/8): gift 128 + credit 50 vs total 375 → credit auto-set to 247 (= gold split); single certificate at wrong amount → set to total; correct 128+247 → unchanged; two non-credit methods with wrong sum → still RAISES the actionable error. payment_history re-synced to charged amounts (verified stored amounts match adjusted, not the pre-adjust 999/171).
- list_reservations (task 17/22): "omar_rossi_1241" → returns FQ8APE (the gold reservation) alongside the others, each with origin/destination/dates/cabin/pax. tau2 builds the JSON schema; output is JSON-serializable.
- Registration: all 15 tools still register (names verified); get_reservation_details and other tools unchanged.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel: serial (single agent). Diagnosis via a small trace parser (user turns + agent tool calls + gold action_checks + feedback) and controlled tool-body runs in the tau2 venv (`/vol/home/skillberry/.cache/capevolve-ci/venv-skillberry-tau2/bin/python3`). The current time is 2024-05-15 15:00:00 EST.

As an airline agent, you can help users **book**, **modify**, or **cancel** flight reservations. You also handle **refunds and compensation**.

Before taking any actions that update the booking database (booking, modifying flights, editing baggage, changing cabin class, or updating passenger information), you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed.

You should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments.

Each user has a profile containing:
